description: A real bridge on a second book. The Cricket warns that boys who run away from home will be sorry; a chapter later, starving and alone, Pinocchio says the Cricket was right. The shared structure is a warning and its vindication; the difference is that Pinocchio reaches it through hunger, not persuasion.

input.cue: Pinocchio keeps saying the Talking Cricket was right. What did the Cricket actually say, and why does it land now?

tool_evidence.excerpt: The Talking Cricket warns that boys who disobey their parents and run away from home will never be happy and will be sorry for it.
Alone and starving, Pinocchio wails that the Talking Cricket was right and that it was wrong to disobey his father and run away.

book_judgement.strength_reason: Two passages were retrieved within the permitted chapters.

criteria: Uses both the warning and the later admission
Names how the admission differs from the warning, not only that they match
forbidden_claims: Claims evidence from beyond the permitted chapters
